display.title: Episode 351: Yaakov's Ladder and Little Avraham (Parshas Vayeitzei)
display.summary_short: Parshas Vayeitzei: why the angels on Yaakov's ladder went up first, a second-grade class sings about the extra Shabbos neshamah, and little Avraham searches for the Creator.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Parshas Vayeitzei 5749, the seventh parsha of the Torah. Uncle Yossi tells of Yaakov Avinu's dream of a ladder reaching from earth to heaven, and asks the Zohar's question: why did the angels go up first and then come down? The Zohar answers that the ladder is the ladder of tefillah: our words of davening become angels that rise to Hashem, and Hashem's brachos come back down the same ladder. Yaakov slept on Har HaMoriah, the place of the first two Batei HaMikdash and of the third, which will be built when Moshiach comes. After the Hakochainik march and the sponsor, a second-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school sings a song they learned about the neshamah yeseirah, the extra soul Hashem gives us on Shabbos, and then leads the Shema. Story time retells the tale of little Avraham, three years old, who looks at the sun, the moon and the stars and realizes that only the one unseen God created them all; he grows up to teach the whole world about Hashem.
display.lesson: Our words of prayer become angels that rise to Hashem and bring His blessings back down, and Hashem, though unseen, is everywhere.
